**Clearer drive cards.** A locked drive's card has **Unlock** and a **More**
menu with each action spelled out, instead of a row of unlabelled icons and
a Remove button that was cut off on Windows.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.4.1-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.4.1-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## Changed

- **Drive cards:** a locked drive shows **Unlock** and **More ▾**, which
  holds **Back up recovery files…**, **Turn back into a plain folder…** and
  **Remove from list (keeps the folder)**. An unlocked drive shows **Open**
  and **Lock**; back it up from Settings → Recovery, or from its card once
  it's locked.

## Known limitations

- Converting a folder and turning a drive back haven't been tried on a real
  Mac yet (they're tested on Windows, and the engine's tests pass on macOS
  and Linux).
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
